claims.text: An NNP trained on a wide ensemble of high-temperature ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations will better capture liquid-state atomic diversity than TOR-TILD EAM references.
Better representation of liquid-state atomic diversity will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The NNP reference will reduce TI path mismatch by approximately a factor of two relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
The relevant initial states are multicomponent high-entropy-alloy liquids at temperatures approximately Tm ± 50–100 K.
An NNP trained on high-temperature liquid ab initio MD snapshots can serve as the reference potential in TI calculations.
The proposed method is applicable to both solid and liquid multicomponent high-entropy alloys near Tm ± 50–100 K.
SOAP or ACSF descriptors can represent short- and mid-range atomic order.
Explicit descriptor-based atomic representations will ensure diverse configurational sampling.
Training data that comprehensively cover configurational space at and above the melting point will allow the NNP to mirror the ab initio distribution of states.
Mirroring the ab initio state distribution will enhance reference–target phase-space overlap.
Enhanced phase-space overlap will reduce TI path mismatch relative to EAM references.
EAM references inadequately capture the atomic diversity of high-temperature multicomponent liquids.
The NNP-based method will achieve free-energy deviations below approximately 5 meV/atom relative to full ab initio TI calculations.
TOR-TILD EAM reference potentials currently exhibit significant TI path mismatch because they incompletely represent liquid configurations.
The method may fail when the training data do not cover the full relevant configurational space.
Scaling to larger system sizes may limit the method's applicability.
Approximately 100 ps trajectories are sufficiently long to capture the relevant configurational diversity.
